title: Internal Version row says 1 while the file family is at version 2
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
description: The metadata table gives Version 1 and the date 28 October 2026, while the file name is v2. Template and Rules R8.2 takes the next version from the highest v<n> of the family, so the new file is v3 and the internal Version row is set to 3. The version 1 value is the only source value that changes, and it is recorded here.
evidence: Metadata table: | Version | 1 |; file name: Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx.
proposed: Treat the file family version (2) as the document version and issue version 3; keep the 28 October 2026 date as the source date; record the mismatch here instead of editing the source.

title: The agent platform of DL33 is never named as a service
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
section: 1. How models reach the Workbench; 4. The large language model endpoint
description: Version 2 says agents call the model endpoint through the agent platform (DL33) and through its tool gateway, but never names the platform as a service, a task queue or an owner. The realignment maps it to rwb-agent (P10, wave 1) from Architecture v5 slide 16 and the Ownership Map.
evidence: Section 1: calls the model endpoint through the agent platform (DL33). Section 4: Reached only through the agent platform's tool gateway. Architecture v5 slide 16: P10 rwb-agent IN Temporal AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result; Tool gateway: read-only calls for the agent.
proposed: Name rwb-agent (P10) as the agent platform of DL33 and its task queue rwb-agent as the only place a model call is made; no other service and no workflow code calls the endpoint.

title: Owner and table of the model version in force are not stated
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
section: 2. Inputs and outputs; 3. Changing a model without a release
description: Version 2 makes the model version in force for each decision step reference data, and the champion and challenger shares part of the same table, but it names neither the table nor its owner and does not say whether the rule package registry of rwb-decision holds it. The R3 default ruling puts parameters and reference data with P3 rwb-case and the rule package registry with P7 rwb-decision.
evidence: Section 3: The model version in force for each decision step is reference data; the center of excellence loads the change and Risk approves it. Champion and challenger runs are set by the same table. Template and Rules R3 default rulings: parameters and reference data E1-042, E1-043 to P3 rwb-case; rule package registry to P7 rwb-decision. Ownership Map Parameters sheet: parameters P3, reference data P3.
proposed: Read the model version in force and the champion and challenger shares as reference data owned by rwb-case (P3) and reached through its reference-data contract (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON); keep the rule package registry with rwb-decision (P7). Leave the table name as the R9 placeholder.

title: INT-08 is not carried in Architecture v5 or the interface set
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
section: 1. How models reach the Workbench; 2. Inputs and outputs
description: Version 2 reads the score output from the daily COLLINS load (INT-08). Architecture v5 names INT-14, INT-19 and INT-20 (removed), INT-23, INT-25 and INT-34, and does not name INT-08. Architecture v5 states instead that ACE ingests COLLINS overnight into the ACE database and that rwb-source-data is the only reader of the recovery.v_ace_* views.
evidence: Section 1: reads their output from the daily COLLINS load (INT-08). Architecture v5 slide 24: ACE ingests all source systems (COLLINS, ALS, CCMS, ...) into the ACE database overnight; Recovery loads no source data itself. Architecture v5 appendix: Interface Specifications v3 (INT-14, INT-19/20 removed, INT-23, INT-25, INT-34).
proposed: Keep INT-08 as written and read it as the ACE overnight ingestion of COLLINS, whose output rwb-source-data (P1) reads through v_ace_score. The owner of the INT-08 interface in the target is the R9 placeholder until the interface register names it.

title: The tool gateway's target systems are not named
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
description: Version 2 says the model endpoint is reached only through the agent platform's tool gateway but does not say which systems the gateway reaches. Architecture v5 slide 16 names two read-only tools for rwb-agent: case facts from source data and extracted fields from documents.
evidence: Section 4: Reached only through the agent platform's tool gateway. Architecture v5 slide 16: REST Source data: tool: read case facts; Document: tool: read extracted fields. AI and Agent Architecture v2 slide 8: the gateway holds the permissions; the agent holds no credential.
proposed: Name the two read-only tools of rwb-agent: case facts and score through the data-product contract of rwb-source-data (P1), and extracted document fields through the REST contract of rwb-document (P5).

title: The monitoring rows name governance roles only, with no service owner for the data
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
description: The monitoring table names Data steward, Model Risk and Center of excellence and never names the service that owns the data each measure reads. The Ownership Map gives an owner to every table, event and data product, so the document can name the data owner without changing the roles.
evidence: Section 5 table: Measure | Owner | Reviewed, with owners Data steward, Model Risk and Center of excellence. Ownership Map: agent_* tables P10, decision_log_entry and approval P7, score read through rwb-source-data P1 (DP-05, ADR-010).
proposed: Keep the three roles word for word and add the data owner of each measure from the Ownership Map: score coverage P1, drift P10 and P7, outcome P1 and P7.

title: D5.1 and D5.2 are not defined and no owning service is assigned
source: 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx
section: 1. How models reach the Workbench, TDR scheme suggester row
description: The TDR scheme suggester row says it is used by D5.1 and D5.2. Neither reference is defined in the document, and the service that runs those steps is not stated, so the realignment keeps the reference as written and assigns no service to it.
evidence: Model table row: TDR scheme suggester | CRR_RET_372 Mortgage, CRR_RET_373 SSME | ... | ACE and COLLINS | D5.1, D5.2.
proposed: Keep D5.1 and D5.2 as written and leave the owning service open; when the treatment decision steps are numbered in the FSD, name the step owner.
